New driver bench/interleaved.js runs inside ONE container (graphtest:1, CPU set 12,14,16,18,20,22, 6 CPUs, 6 GB, empty tmpfs over /build/sealed and /build/audit, repository read-only, stores on the container filesystem). It keeps one persistent warm worker per engine and changes the thread setting at run time. A LadybugDB store opened read-write admits only one process, so one worker per engine is the only form that is the same for all three engines. Idle workers wait on their IPC channel and use no CPU.

Rounds: one round = one query class x one chunk of 20 seeds. Inside a round the three engines run one after another, in an order that cycles through all six permutations, each at 1 thread and at its best setting. Each block takes, per seed: one warm call, one call with the application caches dropped, and one instrumented call (wall and CPU time inside the engine client calls, statements, statement texts), then 50 no-op statements to estimate the round-trip cost. The first block of each class in a worker is preceded by an untimed warm-up pass, and every block starts with one untimed call.

Cold samples (a fresh process: open + first call), store builds (a fresh process), the one-file update (the steps of update.js, with fingerprint and answer checks afterwards) and the LadybugDB harness form (its child process's CPU read from /proc schedstat) all run in alternating blocks too.
Every measure is recorded in wall time and in CPU time of the process doing the work (process.cpuUsage covers every thread, so DuckDB's and LadybugDB's engine threads are included).

Load per block: the driver samples the VM every second (/proc/stat minus this container's cgroup cpu.stat, plus steal) and reads the host timeline, corrected by a clock offset that the host script measures every 5 min. Other work = host processes outside the VM + VM work outside this container. A block taken while other work used more than 12 of the 24 logical CPUs is repeated up to 3 times, then the last attempt is kept and flagged. Every attempt is one line of blocks.jsonl.
Thread calibration runs once, interleaved, and is stored in calibration.json (same rule as before: the fewest threads within 3 % of the lowest median wall time).

refute:claims.verdict:
The held-out numbers reproduce exactly, and the wording rule was applied correctly to every verdict. Most headline sentences still need a qualification. My own scorer re-scored every stored answer of 13 runs (each an arm and role) on T1, T2, T3 and T4, which is 688 tasks per run at 4 budgets: all 35,776 values equal the grader's. My own bootstrap generator reproduces each interval to within 0.003 recall. One sentence in the grader's notes is wrong: "the typed arms lose 4 of the 7 touched questions outright". They lose 2 of them, win 1 and tie 4.

The claim that does not survive as a general statement is "the typed store beats search and the co-change floor". The whole T1 advantage comes from changes whose seed is in the mobile app. Outside the mobile app, the typed stores minus search is +0.024 recall [-0.024, 0.074] and minus the co-change floor is +0.001 [-0.051, 0.055]. The share of mobile-seeded tasks rose from 17 % on TUNE to 36 % on held-out. The "search" arm is close to the co-change floor: about half of its credited recall comes from co-change padding, and it does not beat that floor (-0.013 [-0.032, 0.006]). The typed configuration contains co-change edges itself. On the stored explanation paths, half of its credited recall (0.337 of 0.670 per task) was reached through a path that includes a co-change edge.

"The engines are equivalent" (H1, H2) is true only as "three implementations compute the same answers", which holds by construction. H1b (LadybugDB's native best form against relational) is "equivalent" for the stored community draw only. For community draw 1 the same rule gives "inconclusive", and on T2 the interval is not inside plus or minus 0.05.

The question comparison (H4) is correctly reported as inconclusive. The token gap there (median 31 against 695 tokens) comes mostly from how tokens are counted: search's final answers have a median of 29.5 tokens.
